statements.status_notes: BusyBox wget through 1.37 accepted raw CR, LF and other C0 control bytes in the HTTP request-target, allowing the request line to be split and attacker-controlled headers to be injected.
statements.impact_statement: The flaw is request-target injection in BusyBox wget, a client-side HTTP utility. The platform never runs busybox wget: the web image entrypoint (which starts the Node.js server) and the migrate image entrypoint (which starts Liquibase) contain no wget, curl or busybox call, and neither image defines a HEALTHCHECK. The vulnerable code is therefore never executed.

statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.17.0 until 1.20.0, the fetch adapter bypasses the maxRedirects: 0 redirect policy. An Axios request uses the fetch adapter with maxRedirects set to zero and receives a redirect response. The underlying fetch implementation follows the redirect instead of returning the redirect response unchanged. The redirected request can access internal responses or reach state-changing internal endpoints despite redirects being disabled. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.0.
statements.impact_statement: Axios 1.18.1 is shipped in the api and llt runtime bundle, but the platform does not make runtime axios requests. The only non-test axios usage is importing AxiosError for exception mapping, so the fetch-adapter request path that mishandles maxRedirects is never executed.

statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 0.28.0 until 0.34.0 and 1.15.1 until 1.20.0, ToFormData processes inherited serialization options and visitor properties supplied through prototype pollution. A separate same-process prototype-pollution flaw supplies inherited dots, indexes, metaTokens, maxDepth, visitor, or Blob values before object serialization. The inherited options alter toFormData field naming and data interpretation, maxDepth can force request failure, Blob changes value handling, and a polluted visitor can execute when an attacker already has the stronger ability to inject a function. Serialized field naming and data interpretation can change, maxDepth can cause request failure, Blob can alter value handling, and a polluted visitor can execute under the stronger function-injection primitive. This issue is fixed in versions 0.34.0 and 1.20.0.
statements.impact_statement: Axios 1.18.1 is shipped in the api and llt runtime bundle, but the platform does not make runtime axios requests. The only non-test axios usage is importing AxiosError for exception mapping, so the toFormData serialization path is not exercised by the deployed workload.

statements.status_notes: libstdc++ reallocates storage when erase_if runs on a binary heap priority queue but leaves its internal entry pointer on the old block, so later use reads freed memory.
statements.impact_statement: The affected code is in the C++ standard library's container internals. The Node.js runtime in the api and llt images links no GCC runtime library at all. Both native add-ons the images carry do link libstdc++, but reading the symbols they import shows only red-black tree helpers, the random device and the exception-throw helpers, with no heap or priority-queue symbol in either, so erase_if on a binary-heap priority queue is not linked into anything the platform runs.

statements.status_notes: brace-expansion can exhaust the native stack while expanding a crafted brace pattern, ending the process that expands it.
statements.impact_statement: The package is present in the api and llt images at a release below the fix. It arrives underneath the native add-on build tool's file-matching dependency, and the platform never runs that tool or calls a file-matching helper at run time. Expanding a brace pattern is therefore something no shipped code path does, and no caller can supply a pattern to expand.

statements.status_notes: brace-expansion can exhaust the native stack while expanding deeply nested brace groups, ending the process that expands it.
statements.impact_statement: The package is present in the api and llt images at a release below the fix. It arrives underneath the native add-on build tool's file-matching dependency, and the platform never runs that tool or calls a file-matching helper at run time. The platform ships engine.io through socket.io, but the websocket service is configured to allow only the websocket transport. The published issue requires a transport upgrade on an existing Engine.IO session so that a second transport can negotiate a mismatched protocol revision. Because the platform does not enable polling or transport upgrades, that precondition is not met.

statements.status_notes: Passing an effectively empty string to the ,ccs= syntax extension of the mode argument in the fopen function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled.
statements.impact_statement: The overflow requires an attacker-controlled fopen mode string that uses the glibc-specific ",ccs=" extension. Node.js performs file I/O through libuv with open(2), not fopen. The binaries in the api and llt images that do call fopen use fixed mode strings, and none of them contains a "ccs=" mode, so no request input can reach the vulnerable parser.

statements.status_notes: Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding.
statements.impact_statement: strfmon and strfmon_l are C monetary-formatting functions with no Node.js binding. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of strfmon or strfmon_l, so no platform code path can call them.

statements.status_notes: Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may crash the application.
statements.impact_statement: The tdelete/tsearch binary-tree functions have no Node.js binding. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of tdelete, tsearch, tfind or twalk.

statements.status_notes: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.
statements.impact_statement: The system zlib1g library is installed in the base image but nothing in the api or llt image loads it: Node.js bundles its own zlib, and no glibc-linked binary in the images links against or dynamically loads libz.so.1. The vulnerable crc32_combine64 / crc32_combine_gen64 code in the system package is therefore never executed.

statements.status_notes: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail to enforce the caller-supplied buffer length, and can result in an out-of-bounds write when printing TSIG records.
statements.impact_statement: ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery are deprecated resolver print functions with no Node.js binding. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of any of them. Name resolution goes through getaddrinfo and c-ares, which do not use these functions.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL can hold a QUIC packet buffer for longer than it needs to, letting a remote peer decide how long that memory stays allocated.
statements.impact_statement: The Alpine libcrypto3 package sits in the web and migrate images but nothing in either image loads it. The web image runs Node.js, which bundles its own OpenSSL and links no system TLS library, and its QUIC support is absent entirely. The migrate image runs the Liquibase Java CLI, which uses the JDK's own TLS implementation; the only binaries that link the system library there are the BusyBox TLS helper and the package manager, neither of which serves TLS or speaks QUIC. The QUIC packet-buffer retention path is therefore never executed.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL 3.5.7 and related releases can retain QUIC packet buffers longer than necessary, allowing a malicious peer to force excessive memory usage.
statements.impact_statement: The libssl3t64 package sits in the Debian base for the api and llt images and nothing loads it. The Node.js binary links neither libssl nor libcrypto, it bundles its own OpenSSL, and neither native add-on in those images links them either. The platform also has no QUIC stack at all, so the packet-buffer retention path is doubly out of reach.

statements.status_notes: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.0.1 to version 2.43 fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA length in a DNS response when processing A6, CERT, LOC, TKEY or TSIG records.
statements.impact_statement: Same deprecated resolver print functions as CVE-2026-5435 (ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, fp_nquery), which have no Node.js binding. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of any of them.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in glibc wordexp when it is called with WRDE_APPEND. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of wordexp or wordfree, so the vulnerable code is never executed.

statements.status_notes: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde followed by a username, the internal parse_tilde function of glibc wordexp allocates memory for the username on the stack with strndupa, and an overly long username can cause a stack-based buffer clash.
statements.impact_statement: wordexp performs shell-style word expansion and has no Node.js binding. A review of the dynamic symbols of every glibc-linked binary in the api and llt images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found no import of wordexp or wordfree, so the vulnerable tilde-expansion code is never executed.

statements.status_notes: A TLS server that calls SSL_set_SSL_CTX() to switch a connection to a different SSL_CTX during a handshake may read or write beyond an internal array when the replacement context knows about more provider signature algorithms than the original context.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL QUIC did not enforce connection-level flow control for streams. A malicious remote peer could send data that stayed within per-stream limits while exceeding the intended connection-level cap, causing the stack to allocate far more memory than expected and enabling denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The system libssl3t64 package is present in the distroless Debian base of the api and llt images, but the platform does not use OpenSSL's QUIC stack. Runtime transport code uses Node's standard HTTPS and TLS modules for outbound HTTP, Redis TLS and PostgreSQL TLS, and the only direct native add-on dependency is better-sqlite3, which is a local SQLite binding rather than a QUIC implementation. The vulnerable QUIC flow control path is therefore not reachable from the shipped workload.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The SHIFT_JISX0213 decoder is reached only through glibc iconv. Node.js decodes text with its bundled ICU, not glibc iconv. The only binary in the api and llt images that imports glibc iconv is libvips, which ships with the sharp image library as a transitive dependency of another package. The api and llt services never load sharp, and nothing in the platform requests a SHIFT_JISX0213 conversion, so the vulnerable decoder is never executed.

statements.status_notes: zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall.
statements.impact_statement: The system zlib1g library is installed in the base image but nothing in the api or llt image loads it. Node.js statically bundles its own zlib (process.versions.zlib), and a review of every glibc-linked binary in the images (the Node.js runtime and all native modules) found none that links against or dynamically loads libz.so.1. The vulnerable gz_vacate path is also reached only through the gzFile streaming-write API (gzprintf/gzvprintf after a write stall), which the platform does not use.

statements.status_notes: Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly 200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26 to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the process.
statements.impact_statement: The resolver is in the execution path: Node.js resolves host names through getaddrinfo. The process aborts only when /etc/resolv.conf (or LOCALDOMAIN) contains a search list with a domain of roughly 200 or more characters. That file is written by the deployer's host or orchestrator, never by the platform, and no request input can change it. Impact is denial of service only, with no code execution or data exposure.

statements.status_notes: A time-of-check to time-of-use race condition in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to escalate privileges when $ORIGIN is expanded in DT_RPATH for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.
statements.impact_statement: The attack requires a setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE) program whose run path uses $ORIGIN, so that the dynamic loader can be raced into loading attacker-controlled code. The api and llt images contain no setuid or setgid binaries, so the elevated-privilege load path cannot be entered.

statements.status_notes: The nscd service in the GNU C Library 2.3.4 onwards may crash due to a stack overflow when a malicious DNS server returns too large a response for a DNS query, resulting in degraded DNS resolution for the system.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerability is in the nscd name service caching daemon. nscd is not installed in the api or llt images (they are distroless, Node.js runs as the only process and there is no init system), so the vulnerable daemon code is never executed.

statements.status_notes: proxy-addr before 2.0.8 compiles an IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet with a short prefix, or any IPv6 trust subnet with zero leading bits, into a value that matches every IPv4 address instead of the block it names. Every unauthenticated client is then trusted as a proxy, so the address the application reads from a request is whatever the client sends in X-Forwarded-For. The misconfiguration compiles without error.
statements.impact_statement: The flaw needs the application to hand proxy-addr a trust subnet written as an IPv6 address with zero leading bits, such as `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8` or `::/1`, which compiles to match every client. The platform enables proxy trust as a plain boolean rather than a subnet list, and exposes no setting, environment variable or configuration file that lets a deployment supply one, so the subnet-compilation path the flaw lives in is never entered.

statements.status_notes: http-cache-semantics through 4.2.0 can treat a request carrying a max-stale directive as satisfiable from a stored response that the cache should have revalidated, so a cache shared between users may return one user's stored response to another.
statements.impact_statement: The flaw needs an HTTP response cache that serves stored responses to more than one user. The platform makes its outbound HTTP calls through undici and the native fetch API, neither of which uses this library, and it runs no shared response cache. The copy in the image arrives only underneath command-line and native-build tooling, which no request path invokes.

statements.status_notes: source-map-js before 1.2.2 can spend unbounded time in the event loop when it parses an indexed source map whose sections carry crafted offsets, stalling the process that parses it.
statements.impact_statement: Reaching the flaw means parsing a source map whose section offsets an attacker chose. The library is present underneath CSS build tooling, which runs when the web assets are compiled and not in any shipped request path. The api and llt runtimes have no CSS pipeline and parse no source maps, and nothing lets a caller submit one.

statements.status_notes: libstdc++ can overflow an internal size computation in its container code, corrupting adjacent memory.
statements.impact_statement: The affected code is in the C++ standard library's container internals. The Node.js runtime in the api and llt images links no GCC runtime library at all. Both native add-ons the images carry do link libstdc++, but reading the symbols they import shows only red-black tree helpers, the random device and the exception-throw helpers, with no heap or priority-queue symbol in either, so the same libstdc++ container internals is not linked into anything the platform runs.

statements.status_notes: A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs whose DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with $ORIGIN.
statements.impact_statement: The overflow is in the dynamic loader when it starts a setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE) program whose run path begins with $ORIGIN. The api and llt images contain no setuid or setgid binaries, so a local attacker has no AT_SECURE program to start and the vulnerable loader path is never entered.

statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.13.0 until 1.20.0, Axios HTTP/2 request setup does not consistently apply proxy settings and caller-supplied DNS lookup policy. An HTTPS request that uses httpVersion: 2 can bypass the configured proxy route or the caller-supplied DNS resolution policy before http2.connect().
statements.impact_statement: The platform ships axios in the api and llt runtime dependency graph, but the shipped runtime does not use axios to make outbound requests. The only non-test source reference imports AxiosError for an exception filter; it does not create an axios client, perform a request, follow redirects, or enable HTTP/2. The vulnerable HTTP/2 adapter path is therefore not executed.

statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.13.0 until 1.20.0, Http2Sessions does not install adequate error handling for a ClientHttp2Session during Axios HTTP/2 session initialization or reuse. An unhandled session error can terminate the Node.js process and cause denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The platform ships axios in the api and llt runtime dependency graph, but the shipped runtime does not use axios to make outbound requests. statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.16.1 until 1.20.0, the RFC 2397 regular expression in fromDataURI allows slash characters on both sides of the media-type separator. Malformed attacker-controlled data URLs can trigger excessive backtracking, block the Node.js event loop, and cause denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The platform ships axios in the api and llt runtime dependency graph, but the shipped runtime does not use axios to make outbound requests. The only non-test source reference imports AxiosError for an exception filter; it does not create an axios client, perform a request, or pass untrusted URLs into axios. The vulnerable data: URL parsing path is therefore not executed.

statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.15.2 until 1.20.0, the Node HTTP adapter supplies request options without an own createConnection value. In a process that is already affected by a separate prototype-pollution flaw, Node can invoke an inherited createConnection socket factory and route requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
statements.impact_statement: The platform ships axios in the api and llt runtime dependency graph, but the shipped runtime does not use axios to make outbound requests. The only non-test source reference imports AxiosError for an exception filter; it does not create an axios client or hand request options to the Node HTTP adapter. statements.status_notes: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. From 1.15.0 until 1.20.0, shouldBypassProxy applies a quadratic trailing-dot regular expression to redirect hostnames. Crafted redirect Location values can block the Node.js event loop and cause denial of service when proxy environment variables and NO_PROXY handling are in use.
statements.impact_statement: The platform ships axios in the api and llt runtime dependency graph, but the shipped runtime does not use axios to make outbound requests. The only non-test source reference imports AxiosError for an exception filter; it does not create an axios client, follow redirects, or evaluate NO_PROXY handling for axios requests. The vulnerable redirect and proxy-bypass path is therefore not executed.

statements.status_notes: The Node.js `ImageResponse` implementation from `next/og` is affected by an upstream vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution when an application passes attacker-controlled values into SVG content, attributes, or styles during image generation.
statements.impact_statement: The api, llt and web images all carry Next.js, and none of them uses the Node.js `ImageResponse` implementation from `next/og`. The runtime code defines page metadata only and exposes no `next/og`, `ImageResponse`, `opengraph-image` or `twitter-image` route, so attacker-controlled input cannot reach the affected SVG image-generation path in any image.

statements.status_notes: sharp before 0.35.5 bundles a librsvg build with a memory-handling flaw that, under certain runtime conditions on glibc-based Linux, can lead to remote code execution while rendering SVG input.
statements.impact_statement: The api and llt images carry sharp 0.35.4 and the libvips binaries it bundles, below the 0.35.5 release that picks up the fixed librsvg. It arrives as an optional dependency of Next.js, and nothing in those images imports sharp or renders an SVG: the only Next.js surface that would load it is the image optimizer, which those images do not serve. The web image removes sharp from the standalone output before the runtime image is assembled, so it does not carry the affected code at all.
